1. PURPOSE

This document records the formal service region of the Harbourside Library Network (HLN), the
organisational structure under which the Network operates, and the governance arrangements that
apply to the provision of public library services across the region. It is the authoritative
reference for service boundaries, branch responsibilities, and community planning purposes.

The governance records state that Harbourside Library Network has_service_region Harbourside City. Record status: current.
This declaration of service region is current as at the date of issue of this document and is
reviewed annually by the Board.

2. SERVICE REGION

2.1 Declared service region

The service region of the Harbourside Library Network is Harbourside City. The Network provides
public library services to all residents, ratepayers, and visitors within the municipal boundary
of Harbourside City, as defined by the Local Government Act and the Harbourside City Council
constitution.

The service region includes the following suburbs and localities:

- Harbourside Central (CBD and waterfront precinct)
- North Harbour
- South Harbour
- East Point
- Westfield
- Mariner's Reach
- Saltwater Flats
- Pelican Point
- The Basin
- Harbourview Heights
- Old Quay
- Lighthouse Hill
- Canning Cove
- Tidal Flats
- Riverside Estate
- Dune Park
- Jetty End

2.2 Service boundary notes

The western boundary of the service region follows the Harbourside City Council boundary along
the Marram River, from the river mouth at Pelican Point to the weir at Riverside Estate. The
eastern boundary is the coastline of the Southern Ocean, including all foreshore reserves managed
by the Council. The northern boundary is the ridgeline of the Harbourview Range, and the southern
boundary is the industrial canal at Tidal Flats.

A map of the service region is maintained by the Network's Planning and Partnerships team and is
available on request. The map is updated when Council boundary adjustments are gazetted.

3. ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE

3.1 Governance overview

The Harbourside Library Network operates as a department of the Harbourside City Council under
the Library Act and the Council's Delegations of Authority. The Network is governed by the
Harbourside Library Network Board of Governance, which reports to the Council's Community
Services Committee.

The Board comprises:

- One Councillor (nominated by the Council)
- The Director of Community Services (ex officio)
- Four community representatives (appointed by the Council for a two-year term)
- One representative of the Friends of Harbourside Libraries (non-voting)

The Board meets bi-monthly. Meeting minutes are public documents and are published on the
Network's website within 30 days of each meeting.

3.2 Office of the Director

The Director of the Harbourside Library Network is responsible for the day-to-day operation of
all branches and services. The Director reports to the Board and to the Director of Community
Services.

As at the date of issue, the Director is Ms. A. Whitfield. The previous Director, Mr. R.
Castellan, retired in December 2024 after 12 years of service. The transition was managed
smoothly, and no changes to service delivery resulted.

3.3 Branch structure

The Network operates eight permanent branches and one mobile library service. The branch
locations are as follows:

The mobile library service visits all suburbs on a fortnightly roster. The roster is published
on the Network's website and at each branch.
4. SERVICE DELIVERY POINTS

4.1 Branch directory

The Network’s eight permanent branches are listed below with their standard opening hours. Hours
are reviewed annually and may be adjusted during school holidays or for staff development days.
Notice of any temporary closure is published on the Network’s website and social media channels at
least seven days in advance, except in the case of emergency closures.

| Branch | Address | Opening Hours (Standard) |

| Central Library | 12 Harbour Esplanade, Harbourside | Mon–Fri 9.00–18.00; Sat 9.00–16.00; Sun 12.00–16.00 |
| Pelican Point | 3 Shorebird Lane, Pelican Point | Mon, Wed, Fri 10.00–17.00; Sat 9.00–13.00 |
| Riverside Estate | 45 Weir Road, Riverside Estate | Tue, Thu 10.00–18.00; Sat 9.00–12.00 |
| Harbourview Heights | 78 Lookout Drive, Harbourview Heights | Mon–Fri 10.00–17.00; Sat 9.00–13.00 |
| Tidal Flats | 19 Canal Street, Tidal Flats | Mon, Tue, Thu 10.00–17.00; Wed 12.00–19.00; Sat 9.00–12.00 |
| Saltmarsh | 6 Estuary Parade, Saltmarsh | Mon–Fri 9.30–17.00; Sat 9.00–13.00 |
| Old Wharf | 2 Dock Road, Old Wharf | Tue, Wed, Fri 10.00–17.00; Sat 10.00–14.00 |
| Gull Point | 14 Seabreeze Avenue, Gull Point | Mon, Thu, Fri 10.00–17.00; Sat 9.00–13.00 |

4.2 Mobile library service

The mobile library service operates on a fortnightly roster and provides a full lending service,
including holds collection and returns. The vehicle is wheelchair accessible and carries a
selection of adult fiction, large print, children’s books, and audiobooks. Requests for items not
held on the vehicle can be placed at any stop and are delivered on the next visit.

The mobile library does not operate on public holidays. When a rostered stop falls on a public
holiday, the stop is moved to the following week. The revised roster is published at least two
weeks before the change takes effect.

4.3 Service standards

All branches provide the following core services:

- Borrowing and returns for books, audiobooks, DVDs, and magazines
- Free Wi-Fi and public access computers (booking required for sessions longer than 30 minutes)
- Printing, scanning, and photocopying (charges apply)
- Holds and inter-branch transfers (free of charge)
- Reader advisory and reference assistance
- Programs for children, young people, and adults (see Section 5)
- Home library service for residents who are unable to visit a branch due to illness, disability,
  or caring responsibilities

5. PROGRAMS AND OUTREACH

5.1 Children’s and youth programs

Storytime sessions are held at all branches on a weekly basis during school terms. Baby Rhyme Time
is offered at Central, Pelican Point, and Saltmarsh. School holiday programs are coordinated
centrally and advertised through the Network’s website, school newsletters, and social media.

The Summer Reading Club runs from December to January each year. Registration is free and open to
children aged 5–12. The club is supported by the Friends of Harbourside Libraries.

5.2 Adult programs

The Network hosts a monthly author talk series at Central Library, usually on the first Thursday
of the month. Tickets are free but must be booked in advance through the website or at any branch.

A digital literacy program, “Tech Help”, is offered at all branches on a rotating basis. Sessions
cover basic computer skills, email, online safety, and using library apps. Bookings are essential.

Book clubs operate independently at several branches. The Network supports these groups by
providing discussion sets and meeting space. Groups interested in joining the Network’s book club
set scheme should contact the Programs team at programs@harbourside.nsw.gov.au.

HARBOURSIDE LIBRARY NETWORK
GOVERNANCE AND SERVICE REGION
Annual Review 2024–2025

Approved by the Harbourside Library Network Board of Governance
Date of issue: 28 February 2025
Next scheduled review: February 2026
Document control: HLN-GOV-2025-01 (supersedes HLN-GOV-2024-01)

---

1. PURPOSE

This document records the formal service region of the Harbourside Library Network (HLN), the
organisational structure under which the Network operates, and the governance arrangements that
apply to the provision of public library services across the region. It is the authoritative
reference for service boundaries, branch responsibilities, and community planning purposes.

The governance records state that Harbourside Library Network has_service_region Harbourside City. Record status: current.
This declaration of service region is current as at the date of issue of this document and is
reviewed annually by the Board.

2. SERVICE REGION

2.1 Declared service region

The service region of the Harbourside Library Network is Harbourside City. The Network provides
public library services to all residents, ratepayers, and visitors within the municipal boundary
of Harbourside City, as defined by the Local Government Act and the Harbourside City Council
constitution.

The service region includes the following suburbs and localities:

- Harbourside Central (CBD and waterfront precinct)
- North Harbour
- South Harbour
- East Point
- Westfield
- Mariner's Reach
- Saltwater Flats
- Pelican Point
- The Basin
- Harbourview Heights
- Old Quay
- Lighthouse Hill
- Canning Cove
- Tidal Flats
- Riverside Estate
- Dune Park
- Jetty End

2.2 Service boundary notes

The western boundary of the service region follows the Harbourside City Council boundary along
the Marram River, from the river mouth at Pelican Point to the weir at Riverside Estate. The
eastern boundary is the coastline of the Southern Ocean, including all foreshore reserves managed
by the Council. The northern boundary is the ridgeline of the Harbourview Range, and the southern
boundary is the industrial canal at Tidal Flats.

A map of the service region is maintained by the Network's Planning and Partnerships team and is
available on request. The map is updated when Council boundary adjustments are gazetted.

3. ORGANISATIONAL STRUCTURE

3.1 Governance overview

The Harbourside Library Network operates as a department of the Harbourside City Council under
the Library Act and the Council's Delegations of Authority. The Network is governed by the
Harbourside Library Network Board of Governance, which reports to the Council's Community
Services Committee.

The Board comprises:

- One Councillor (nominated by the Council)
- The Director of Community Services (ex officio)
- Four community representatives (appointed by the Council for a two-year term)
- One representative of the Friends of Harbourside Libraries (non-voting)

The Board meets bi-monthly. Meeting minutes are public documents and are published on the
Network's website within 30 days of each meeting.

3.2 Office of the Director

The Director of the Harbourside Library Network is responsible for the day-to-day operation of
all branches and services. The Director reports to the Board and to the Director of Community
Services.

As at the date of issue, the Director is Ms. A. Whitfield. The previous Director, Mr. R.
Castellan, retired in December 2024 after 12 years of service. The transition was managed
smoothly, and no changes to service delivery resulted.

3.3 Branch structure

The Network operates eight permanent branches and one mobile library service. The branch
locations are as follows:

The mobile library service visits all suburbs on a fortnightly roster. The roster is published
on the Network's website and at each branch.

4.1 Branch directory

The Network’s eight permanent branches are listed below with their standard opening hours. Hours
are reviewed annually and may be adjusted during school holidays or for staff development days.
Notice of any temporary closure is published on the Network’s website and social media channels at

4.2 Mobile library service

The mobile library service operates on a fortnightly roster and provides a full lending service,
including holds collection and returns. The vehicle is wheelchair accessible and carries a
selection of adult fiction, large print, children’s books, and audiobooks. Requests for items not
held on the vehicle can be placed at any stop and are delivered on the next visit.

The mobile library does not operate on public holidays. When a rostered stop falls on a public
holiday, the stop is moved to the following week. The revised roster is published at least two
weeks before the change takes effect.

4.3 Service standards

All branches provide the following core services:

- Borrowing and returns for books, audiobooks, DVDs, and magazines
- Free Wi-Fi and public access computers (booking required for sessions longer than 30 minutes)
- Printing, scanning, and photocopying (charges apply)
- Holds and inter-branch transfers (free of charge)
- Reader advisory and reference assistance
- Programs for children, young people, and adults (see Section 5)
- Home library service for residents who are unable to visit a branch due to illness, disability,
  or caring responsibilities

5. PROGRAMS AND OUTREACH

5.1 Children’s and youth programs

Storytime sessions are held at all branches on a weekly basis during school terms. Baby Rhyme Time
is offered at Central, Pelican Point, and Saltmarsh. School holiday programs are coordinated
centrally and advertised through the Network’s website, school newsletters, and social media.

The Summer Reading Club runs from December to January each year. Registration is free and open to
children aged 5–12. The club is supported by the Friends of Harbourside Libraries.

5.2 Adult programs

The Network hosts a monthly author talk series at Central Library, usually on the first Thursday
of the month. Tickets are free but must be booked in advance through the website or at any branch.

A digital literacy program, “Tech Help”, is offered at all branches on a rotating basis. Sessions
cover basic computer skills, email, online safety, and using library apps. Bookings are essential.

Book clubs operate independently at several branches. The Network supports these groups by
providing discussion sets and meeting space. Groups interested in joining the Network’s book club
set scheme should contact the Programs team at programs@harbourside.nsw.gov.au.

Venue: Central Library, Program Room 2

Note: The schedule shows Creative Writing Workshop is_offered_at Central Library. Record status: current. This is the current listing for Winter 2024. Please note the venue change from the Spring listing: Program Room 2 is the smaller room on the ground floor, not the Central Neighbourhood Room as previously advertised. M. Chen is the lead facilitator for all Saturday sessions. J. Alvarez will facilitate the first two Saturdays of October (5 and 12 October) while M. Chen is away at a writers' festival. J. Alvarez is not yet on the approved facilitator list — please process her visitor access form before the first session. She has run similar workshops at the Eastside Branch and comes with a strong reference from the regional arts council.

Workshop content rotates on a four-week cycle:
Week 1: Free writing and warm-up exercises
Week 2: Character development and dialogue
Week 3: Editing and revision techniques
Week 4: Open mic reading (voluntary) and peer feedback

Participants are encouraged to bring their own notebooks and writing materials. A small selection of stationery is available from the front desk. The workshop is not a critique group; feedback is given in a supportive and constructive manner. Participants who miss more than two consecutive sessions may be asked to rebook for the next term to keep the group size manageable.
